purpose: Three additional primary scholarly comparators for the selected analytic and probabilistic interfaces. These are substantive precedents, not evidence of empirical rarity.
method: Read publisher bibliographic records and primary full texts through web browsing; retained all three primary PDFs with SHA256 hashes. No manuscript or bibliography file was edited.

references.title: Formalizing the Divergence Theorem and the Cauchy Integral Formula in Lean
references.venue: 13th International Conference on Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP 2022)
references.publisher_metadata_title: Formalizing the Divergence Theorem and the Cauchy Integral Formula in Lean
references.claim_supported: Earlier Lean work already formalizes integration-theory transport and careful regularity interfaces: a GP-integral divergence theorem is transferred to the Bochner integral, and the resulting rectangular-domain theorem yields Cauchy–Goursat without continuity assumptions on the complex derivative.
references.limitation: Its domains are rectangular boxes; it does not establish the sphere-local exact-form flux theorem or ordered differential-form representation used in the Mahler case.
references.closest_comparison: This gives a direct precedent for organizing analysis around the assumptions of an integration interface. Mahler's specific audited bridge concerns sphere-local form congruence and a cutoff extension.
references.suggested_placement: Discussion paragraph beginning 'These patterns have substantial antecedents', or the Mahler subsection's concluding comparison with established formal analysis.

references.title: Proofs of randomized algorithms in Coq
references.publisher_metadata_title: Proofs of randomized algorithms in Coq
references.year_note: The selected reference is the 2009 expanded journal article; its DOI contains 2007, and an earlier conference version appeared in 2006.
references.claim_supported: The Coq development interprets randomized programs as functionals M(A)=(A→[0,1])→[0,1], representing subprobabilities through expectations. It proves probability rules, supports general recursion, and verifies a Bernoulli sampler from coin flips.
references.limitation: This is an expectation-based denotational account, not a cost-bearing compiler theorem for the particular fixed oracle machine and tape positions inspected in CommonBases.
references.closest_comparison: The all-observables output certificate should be presented as a concrete application of established expectation semantics; its case-specific content is the connection to bounded banks and fixed-machine execution.
references.suggested_placement: CommonBases final comparison paragraph, alongside CertiCrypt/EasyCrypt; optionally the discussion's sentence about observations and output distributions.

references.title: Verified Foundations for Differential Privacy
references.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
references.claim_supported: SampCert verifies exact discrete samplers in Lean. Its SLang uses unnormalized mass functions; normalization promotes completed samplers to PMFs. Equal sampler distributions support substituting implementations without redoing downstream privacy proofs.
references.limitation: Section 4.1 explicitly retains external runtime definitions in the trusted computing base; the article does not supply CommonBases' inspected fixed-machine cost and physical-tape theorem.
references.closest_comparison: This is a close Lean precedent for separating executable sampling structure from distribution semantics and using equality of output laws as a downstream interface.
references.suggested_placement: CommonBases final comparison paragraph and discussion of preservation of probability laws; citation should support established sampler/distribution interfaces, not a rarity claim.

proposed_comparison_paragraph: Kudryashov's Lean formalization already transfers a divergence theorem between integration theories and derives Cauchy–Goursat under carefully chosen differentiability assumptions \citep{Kudryashov2022}. Audebaud and Paulin-Mohring establish expectation-functional semantics for randomized Coq programs \citep{AudebaudPaulinMohring2009}, while SampCert separates Lean sampling procedures from normalized distribution semantics and verifies exact discrete samplers \citep{deMedeirosEtAl2025}. These precedents focus the present comparison on the particular sphere-local congruences and fixed-machine tape correspondence, while treating integration interfaces, observation semantics, and verified sampling as established approaches.
proposed_paragraph_placement: discussion.tex, after the current sentences on verified compilers and probabilistic program logics in the paragraph beginning 'These patterns have substantial antecedents'; alternatively use the first sentence in the Mahler case and the second in the CommonBases concluding paragraph, retaining the third in discussion.
novelty_guardrail: These references support positive claims about prior formalized mechanisms. The review neither establishes historical first use nor estimates how frequent the techniques are. Kudryashov is a divergence/complex-analysis comparator, not evidence of a general manifold Stokes formalization.
selection_note: Prioritized a direct Lean integration-theory predecessor and two exact probabilistic-semantic comparators. General smooth-manifold library papers and newer Stokes preprints were not added merely to raise the bibliography count.
